missionPremise: The Settings Access row shipped showing 'Paid' to every account including anonymous (commit b4add1b), and the P-98 next-action rail's annual_upgrade rung shipped starved. BOTH have the same single cause: `GET api/property-explorer/v1/entitlement` could only be asked about a PARCEL, and Settings is account-scoped. A sibling lane in legacy-design-tools is making that GET callable without a parcelNodeId. This lane is the client half: read the account block, light up the three Plan values it can honestly answer, and feed billingInterval into the ladder. The rule the work is judged on is that a NULL interval must never be treated as monthly, because offering 'switch to annual' to an annual subscriber is the failure that rung would be judged on.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this by: (1) confirming `npx vitest run` in apps/property-explorer reports MORE tests than the 2194 baseline with none removed; (2) reading src/lib/account-entitlement-client.test.ts and finding the three-direction violation block (monthly fires, annual does not, null does not) driven from a WIRE BODY rather than a hand-built ladder input; (3) breaking `if (e.billingInterval !== "monthly") return null;` in src/lib/nextAction.ts and confirming tests go red; (4) confirming git reports no modification to usePropertyEntitlement.ts or entitlementClient.ts.
scopeBasis: Bounded to the CLIENT half in hauska-map. The server half is another seat's repo and was READ (to establish today's pre-contract behaviour) but never written. Inside the client, the boundary is the three rows the account entitlement can actually answer — Access, Tier name, Billing interval. Renewal date, Payment method, Invoices and Cancel subscription were deliberately left because they remain genuinely unread or unbuilt, and a test now pins that they were not touched. seatsPurchased is parsed but wired to nothing, deliberately: the Team tab already derives a purchased-seat count from the roster, and a second derivation without a divergence test between them is how two numbers that should agree start disagreeing on screen.

api/spine-deep.ts builds its allowlist key from req.query.upath SEGMENTS ONLY (`path.join('/')`), stripping the query into a separate URLSearchParams. So a deep path needs ONE allowlist line regardless of how many query shapes call it — and adding a query-only variant of an existing GET needs no allowlist change. It also checks the session cookie BEFORE the allowlist, which is why a 403 is only ever visible to a signed-IN request.

A test that pins a STARVATION (here, the literal `billingInterval: null` in the mount) becomes the obstacle to unstarving it. When that happens, keep the anti-invention half verbatim and replace the positive half with one that names the SOURCE of the value. Deleting the whole test is weakening; keeping the literal is ceremony.

hauska-map's PE app has NO DOM or screenshot harness — every component test is renderToStaticMarkup, and effects never run. That makes first-paint assertions cheap and post-read assertions impossible. Push behaviour into PURE EXPORTED FUNCTIONS (accessLabel, ladderEntitlementFromAccount) so the resolved states are testable at all; a value computed inline in JSX is untestable in this repo.
